Corporate Social Responsibility in Coal India Limited: A Journey from Community Welfare to Inclusive Growth
articles.full_content:
Coal India Limited’s CSR Expenditure Rises to Nearly Rs. 1,000 Crore Annually CIL Spends Rs. 7,276 Crore on CSR Against Statutory Requirement of Rs. 5,795 Crore During FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26
For a company whose operations touch some of the most resource-poor and tribal-dominated districts of India, the idea of giving back to the community is not new to Coal India Limited (CIL). Long before the Companies Act, 2013 made Corporate Social Responsibility a legal obligation for corporate India, CIL and its subsidiaries were already engaged in welfare activities in and around their mining areas under the Community Development (CD) Policy, 2005.
Under this earlier CD regime, subsidiaries supported villages within an 8 km radius of mining operations through drinking water facilities, health camps, and small infrastructure works — meaningful interventions that fostered harmony with peripheral communities. In the three years leading up to the Act (FY 2011-12 to 2013-14), CIL's consolidated CD spend varied from Rs. 82 cr. (FY 2011-12) to Rs. 409 cr . (FY 2013-14) . The work being done was genuine and appreciated on the ground; what it lacked was a consistent, institutionalised framework to sustain and scale it year on year.
The Companies Act, 2013 and Section 135 changed this fundamentally. Companies were now required to spend a statutorily defined share of their average net profits on CSR, guided by Schedule VII themes and monitored by a Board-level CSR Committee. CIL built on this with its own policy architecture: at least 80% of annual CSR expenditure within a 25 km radius of mines and establishments, prioritising Project Affected Areas, with the balance for state and national initiatives. As a natural consequence of this local-area focus, more than 90% of CIL's CSR expenditure continues to be incurred within coal-bearing states — keeping the benefit anchored where the impact of mining is felt most directly.
The results are visible in the numbers. CIL has not merely met its statutory obligation — it has exceeded it consistently, year after year. Cumulatively, from FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, CIL has spent Rs. 7,276 crore against a statutory requirement of Rs. 5,795 crore . What is more striking is the trajectory within this: annual expenditure, once closer to Rs. 500 cr., the yearly outlay now touches almost Rs. 1,000 crore — placing CIL among the largest corporate CSR spenders in the country.
This growth in scale has been matched by a growth in purpose, with CIL's CSR converging deliberately with national missions. It was the number one CPSE contributor to the Swachh Vidyalaya Abhiyan, completing over 50,000 toilets in government schools; it was among the earliest major contributors to the PM-CARES Fund and ran an extensive COVID-19 relief programme, from dedicated hospitals in Odisha and Chhattisgarh to oxygen plants under “Mission Praana Vayu.” Flagship interventions have given the programme a distinct identity of its own — the NIRMAN scheme rewarding

articles.full_content:
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia and Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav Chair Investors Roundtable in Bengaluru “24 companies already on board, propose to invest ₹5,500 crore in Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Zone”: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Industry Engagement Focuses on Strengthening Domestic Telecom Manufacturing and Innovation Ecosystem; ~₹700 crores committed in Bengaluru Investor Roadshow for TMZ, Gwalior The establishment of India’s first integrated Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) is in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India Initiative
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) organised its 3 rd Investors’ Roundtable in Bengaluru today to engage with leading technology, telecom, semiconductor and electronics industry stakeholders on investment opportunities in India’s first integrated Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) coming up in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
The roundtable, chaired by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region along with Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh brought together industry leaders and potential investors to deliberate on strengthening domestic telecom manufacturing capabilities, enhancing value addition, promoting research and development, encouraging innovation, supporting exports and developing a globally competitive telecom and electronics ecosystem.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said, “The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a powerful example of cooperative federalism in action. The Union Government and the Madhya Pradesh Government are working hand in hand, with the State putting in place incentives and subsidies of around ₹8,000 crore. This kind of collaborative approach creates the confidence for the private sector to invest, innovate and scale.”
The Union Minister further added, “India is now moving decisively from being a services-led nation to a product-led nation. In telecom, our three priorities are clear: increase domestic value addition, create intellectual property in India, and take Indian-designed and Indian-manufactured products to every corner of the world. We have seen India’s Atmanirbharta journey gather momentum across sectors, from semiconductors to aviation. The next frontier is telecom. Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Make in India, Make for India and Make for the World, we must now also Design in India and build products that compete globally”
The Union Minister also highlighted that, “Today’s Bengaluru roadshow marks the completion of Phase 1 of our investor outreach, with nearly 24 companies already on board. Our commitment is simple: if an investor has a query or faces an issue related to the TMZ, we will work to resolve it within 48 hours. We want to make Gwalior not just a manufacturing destination, but a destination where industry knows it has a responsive governmen

Union Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Interacts with Industry Stakeholders on Ease of Doing Business, FTA Opportunities and Trade Reforms Workshop
articles.full_content:
Shri Goyal Calls for Strengthening Export Facilitation through Physical and Digital Mechanisms Local Personnel Proposed to Strengthen Exporter Support at District and State Levels: Shri Goyal Trade Connect platform envisaged to provide product-wise and HSN-code-wise information on tariffs, FTA opportunities and procedures
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) organised a stakeholder workshop on Ease of Doing Business, Free Trade Agreement opportunities and ongoing trade-related reforms at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today, followed by an interactive session with Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada.
During the interaction, Shri Goyal outlined the Government’s approach to strengthening export facilitation through physical and digital mechanisms. He said that instead of establishing separate offices of every department in every location, integrated Commerce and Industry offices are envisaged in major cities to provide businesses with a common point of access to multiple departments and agencies.
He had a frank interaction with industry representatives and directed officials to examine some of the suggestions made by industry.
The interaction was the first such interaction with a regional industry association.
The roller chain and industrial components manufacturing sector highlighted the positive impact of recent policy interventions in strengthening domestic manufacturing. The industry reported that measures including Quality Control Orders (QCOs), Minimum Import Price (MIP) provisions and higher import duties have supported significant growth in the sector, contributing to a 15-fold expansion, fresh investments of approximately ₹500 crore and the generation of around 5,000 new jobs. The industry appreciated these interventions for supporting domestic manufacturing capacity, encouraging investment and creating employment opportunities.
The Minister also announced a proposed network of approximately 1,000 trained local personnel, with knowledge of regional languages, to support exporters and prospective exporters at the district and State levels. These personnel would be trained and subsequently deployed to provide handholding support to businesses, including through industry chambers and regional associations.
Shri Goyal also informed participants about the Trade Connect platform being developed to provide exporters with product-wise and HSN-code-wise information, including destination-country tariffs, FTA opportunities and procedures for availing FTA benefits. The platform is also envisaged to use digital and AI-enabled tools to help businesses identify potential export opportunities and infrastructure gaps.
The workshop brought together representatives from industry associations, trade bodies and sectoral organisations, along with senior officials of DPIIT and the Department of Commerce. Discussions focused on ongoing EoDB reform

From Skill to Self-Reliance
articles.full_content:
Smt. Shalaka Nagotkar's Entrepreneurial Journey
Professional skills can create meaningful livelihood opportunities when supported by timely and affordable finance. Institutional assistance enables aspiring entrepreneurs to overcome initial financial barriers, establish sustainable enterprises and move towards economic independence.
Smt. Shalaka Darshan Nagotkar, a graduate and trained beauty professional from Kalyan (West), Thane, Maharashtra, established a home-based beauty parlour with financial assistance of Rs. 3,75,000 under the NSFDC Term Loan Scheme. Today, she earns a monthly net income of approximately Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 30,000 and supports her family through her enterprise.
Smt. Shalaka holds a diploma in Beauty Parlour and aspired to use her professional skills to become financially independent. However, she did not own a shop, and the high rent of commercial premises made it difficult for her to start a business.
After learning about NSFDC schemes through the internet, she approached the Thane Branch of the Leather Industries Development Corporation of Maharashtra Limited (LIDCOM). She received financial assistance of Rs. 3,75,000 under the NSFDC Term Loan Scheme. The loan was disbursed on 30 October 2024 to help her establish her own beauty parlour.
To manage the high cost of commercial space, Smt. Shalaka made a practical beginning by operating the beauty parlour from her home in Kalyan (West). The assistance enabled her to purchase the equipment and materials required to provide professional beauty and grooming services.
Through her skills, dedication and consistent efforts, she developed a stable source of livelihood. Her beauty parlour now provides her with a monthly net income of approximately Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 30,000, strengthening her financial independence and helping her support her family.
Smt. Shalaka has expressed her gratitude to NSFDC for the financial assistance provided under the Term Loan Scheme. Her journey demonstrates how professional skills, determination and timely credit support can enable women entrepreneurs to build sustainable livelihoods and become self-reliant.

NSC Approves ₹320 Crore under PM-SETU for Kurukshetra ITI Cluster in Haryana; Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited to Partner in Transformation of Seven ITIs
articles.full_content:
Cumulative PM-SETU investment now reaches ₹2,491 crore across 10 ITI clusters, advancing the creation of modern, industry-led and future-ready vocational training institutions nationwide Bringing Industry Closer to ITIs Will Create Stronger Employment Pathways for Youth: Jayant Chaudhary
The National Steering Committee (NSC) of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has approved a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) worth ₹320 crore for the Kurukshetra ITI Cluster in Haryana under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme. Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited will partner with the Government of Haryana as the Anchor Industry Partner for the cluster.
With this approval, the cumulative investment sanctioned under PM-SETU has risen to ₹2,491 crore across 10 ITI clusters, reinforcing the Government’s commitment to transforming Industrial Training Institutes into industry-led, future-ready centres of excellence that are aligned with evolving workforce requirements.
The approval marks another significant step towards strengthening the industry-led transformation of Government Industrial Training Institutes and creating a more demand-driven vocational training ecosystem.
Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, said: "Bringing industry closer to ITIs will create stronger employment pathways for our youth. The approval of the Kurukshetra cluster under PM-SETU reflects our commitment to making skill development more relevant, aspirational and responsive to the changing needs of industry. Through strong industry partnerships, we are working to ensure that young people are equipped with the skills, exposure and opportunities required to participate meaningfully in India's growth story”.
One Hub and Six Spoke ITIs to be Transformed
The Kurukshetra cluster will be developed under the Hub-and-Spoke model envisaged under PM-SETU and will comprise seven Government ITIs.
Government ITI, Kurukshetra will serve as the Hub ITI, while the following institutes will function as Spoke ITIs:
• Government ITI (Women), Kurukshetra
• Government ITI, Kaithal
• Government ITI (Women), Kaithal
• Government ITI, Pehowa
• Government ITI, Pabnawa
• Government ITI (Women), Ambala City
The ₹320 crore investment will support the development of an integrated and industry-responsive skilling ecosystem across the cluster. The proposed interventions will focus on strengthening infrastructure, modernising training facilities, introducing industry-aligned courses, and enhancing employability outcomes for trainees.
Strengthening Industry-ITI Linkages

Ministry of MSME Gears Up for Special Campaign 6.0 on Swachhata and Disposal of Pendency
articles.full_content:
Ministry has disposed 22,365 Public Grievances and Freed 1,167 Sq. Ft. Space under Special Campaign 5.0
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) is gearing up for Special Campaign 6.0, to be conducted from 2nd to 31st October, 2026 under the aegis of the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG). The Campaign seeks to improve cleanliness and citizen experience across Government offices, with this edition placing added emphasis on “effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste” in line with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, and on field/outstation offices that directly interface with the public, besides Ministries/Departments, their attached and subordinate offices, Autonomous Bodies and PSUs.
A Preparatory Phase (15–30 September, 2026) is currently underway, during which the Ministry is sensitizing offices down to the field level, and drawing up an action plan for the campaign. The subsequent Implementation Phase (2–31 October, 2026) will drive cleanliness, e-waste disposal, digitisation, record weeding, space management, and clearance of pending MP References, State Government references, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, and public grievances.
In Special Campaign 5.0, the Ministry and its organisations — the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi & Village Industries Commission, Coir Board, National Small Industries Corporation, National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, and Mahatma Gandhi Institute for Rural Industrialisation — reviewed 23,162 physical files, weeded out 4,280 files, freed up 21,045 sq. ft. of office space, and disposed of scrap worth ₹22.89 lakh. Over 81% of MP references and 99% of public grievances were cleared, as part of 1,045 cleanliness campaigns conducted during the period.
Further, pursuant to DARPG’s directions to sustain the momentum generated under Special Campaign 5.0, Ministry directed its organisations to undertake activities on various parameters of the Campaign. As a result, during the period from November, 2025 to September 2026, 22,365 Public Grievances, 4850 Public Grievances Appeals, 226 MP references have been disposed; 626 Physical files and 127 E-files have been weeded out after review and around 1167 sq ft. of space has been freed. Moreover, officers of the Ministry have visited its field offices and institutions, to sensitise the staff, and review their performance in the Campaign.
Sensitization workshop at NSIC Branch Office Guwahati
Plantation drive at DFO-Branch officer, Aurangabad
Building on these gains, the Ministry and its organisations remain committed to carry Special Campaign 6.0 forward with the same rigour, towards cleaner and more responsive governance.

Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited will continue to play a central role towards achievement of India’s clean energy vision: Shri Shripad Yesso Naik
articles.full_content:
SECI celebrates its 15th Foundation Day with Stakeholders’ Meet
“SECI's 15-year journey stands as a reflection of India's growing leadership in the global renewable energy transition,” said Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy and Power while addressing the gathering at the celebration of the 15th Foundation Day of Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) here today as the Chief Guest.
Shri Naik said that SECI has consistently delivered on the nation’s clean energy vision and expressed confidence that the corporation will continue to play a central role towards its achievement.
The event was also graced by Shri Ghanshyam Prasad, Chairperson, CEA, Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, MNRE and Shri Vivek Jain, Chairman, INOXGFL Group along with other senior officials of the Renewable Energy sector.
Speaking at the event, Shri Akash Tripathi, Managing Director, SECI, said that SECI remains committed to open new opportunities in the renewable energy sector, working closely with all stakeholders and innovating with market's requirements. These 15 years have been a testament to SECI's dedication and the nation's collective will towards sustainable energy. We are thankful to all our stakeholders for putting their faith in us.
The Stakeholders’ Meet featured two thematic sessions, “Reimagining Industry through Green Molecules” and “The Changing Energy Landscape: Distributed Renewables and New Energy Markets,” bringing together policymakers, industry leaders and financial institutions to deliberate on emerging opportunities and challenges shaping India’s energy transition.
The first session, “Reimagining Industry through Green Molecules,” explored the role of green hydrogen and its derivatives in decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors and creating new avenues for industrial growth. The session covered opportunities for domestic production and emerging applications, along with the policy support, infrastructure, technology and financing required to develop green molecule markets on a scale.
The second session, “The Changing Energy Landscape: Distributed Renewables and New Energy Markets,” examined the evolving role of distributed RE in India. Key areas of discussion included greater consumer participation, integration of distributed energy resources and emerging market mechanisms, as well as the policy and regulatory frameworks needed to facilitate their effective integration and support the expansion of renewable energy.
As SECI marks 15 years of service to the nation, its cumulative achievements stand at over 41 GW of renewable energy generation capacity commissioned through third-party developers, power sale agreements of over 67 GW signed with various DISCOMs/consumers, and cumulative market investments enabled for about ₹3.6 lakh crores. The company is rapidly scaling with its own projects' portfolio as well and is also active in promoting energy storage, green hydrogen and allied areas.

articles.summary: SECI celebrates its 15th Foundation Day with Stakeholders’ Meet “SECI's 15-year journey stands as a reflection of India's growing leadership in the global renewable energy transition,” said Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy and Power while addressing the gathering at the celebration of the 15th Foundation Day of Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) here today as the Chief Guest. Shri Naik said that SECI has consistently delivered on the nation’s clean energy vision and expressed confidence that the corporation will continue to play a central role towards its achievement. The event was also graced by Shri Ghanshyam Prasad, Chairperson, CEA, Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, MNRE and Shri Vivek Jain, Chairman, INOXGFL Group along with other senior officials of the Renewable Energy sector.

As a follow up to Departmental Summit, DDWS Organised First Virtual Conference With States and UTs on Strengthening Skilled Rural Water Workforce Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
articles.full_content:
States/UTs urged to accelerate Nal Jal Mitra and Sujalam Shakti initiatives to build a professional, locally available workforce for sustainable rural water service delivery
The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, today organised the first National Virtual Conference with States and Union Territories, as a follow up to the Departmental Summit ( organized from 1-2 September 2026) to discuss the roadmap for strengthening the skilled rural water workforce required for sustainable operation and maintenance (O&M), water quality surveillance and long-term functionality of rural drinking water infrastructure under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0.
The Conference brought together representatives from State Water and Sanitation Missions, Public Health Engineering Departments, State Skill Development Missions, Rural Development Departments, Panchayati Raj Institutions, Technical Education Departments and other partner institutions working in skilling and technical education.
In his opening remarks, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS , emphasised that the long-term success of Jal Jeevan Mission depends not only on infrastructure creation but also on the availability of trained and skilled human resources to operate, maintain and monitor rural water supply systems. He highlighted the need to establish a structured and professional ecosystem for operation and maintenance to sustain safe and reliable drinking water services in villages.
A major focus of the Conference was the rollout of the Nal Jal Mitra (NJM) programme. Participants were informed that DDWS, in collaboration with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and NCVTE, has developed an NSQF-aligned Nal Jal Mitra qualification for rural drinking water systems. The programme aims to create a cadre of village-level multi-skilled technicians capable of undertaking routine operation, preventive maintenance and first-level repairs of rural water supply infrastructure. Covering skills related to pumps, pipelines, treatment systems, electrical installations and associated infrastructure, the programme forms a key component of DDWS's strategy to build a professional workforce for sustaining rural drinking water systems under JJM 2.0.
States and UTs were briefed on the two implementation pathways under the programme: a 510-hour Short-Term Training course for new entrants and a 120-hour Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) pathway for existing operators, plumbers, electricians, pump attendants and other personnel engaged in rural water supply systems. States were encouraged to leverage both pathways and prioritise local youth to ensure the availability of skilled resources within rural areas while creating livelihood opportunities.
